disposition_reason: Mouse carbonyl-iron diet (25 g/kg) versus chow (180 mg/kg) metabolomics; no food occurrence data.

study.method: Untargeted LC-high-resolution MS of blood (VAMS), plasma and liver
study.qa: Duplicate injections for liver; n = 3 control, 5 iron

regulatory_or_exposure: Control chow 180 mg iron/kg; iron diet supplemented with 25 g carbonyl iron/kg for 14 days (Section 2.2, p. 3)
non_numeric_findings: Iron loading increased glucose, aspartic acid and 2-/3-hydroxybutyric acid and lowered lactate and malate in blood and plasma.
Liver urea cycle stimulated; oxidative stress and liver glutathione increased.
Authors note supra-physiological dietary iron as a limitation.
